agent.problem: Discovery questions dominate the stop rather than remaining a few exceptions. Cards 2, 3, 5, 8 and 15 ask for unrevealed details without setup that favors the right answer, and card 18 likewise introduces rule in Mount Zion forever without enough context to reason it out. Together with the wording-only blanks on cards 6 and 17, most of the choices cannot be reasoned from the earlier cards.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: The earlier cards do not identify the LORD's mountain as Zion or otherwise give the baker a basis for choosing Zion over Sinai. The blank therefore asks for the unrevealed wording of the line rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: This is the only card for Micah 4:5, and rejecting its distorted statement does not tell the baker what the verse actually affirms. The walkthrough moves straight to 4:6 without ever giving the central contrast: though the nations may walk in the names of their gods, Micah's side will walk in the name of the LORD their God forever and ever.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
